name: Edward Roy
life: “I still remember my family's name read wrong over a graduation speaker.” People around the downtown fountain know Edward by a small Thursday habit. Edward keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I once changed my name to make school easier. I will pronounce hers however she asks.
appearance: Edward is easy to recognize by black hair twisted into a small knot and a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Usually dressed in an olive canvas jacket with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead, Edward takes off the watch before a long conversation when listening.
personality: Edward talks very little about private fear and recognizes it quickly in strangers. Offering a choice of seats is one of Edward's ways of saying that it is all right to leave.
family: Kai Berry is Edward’s stepsibling. Edward calls about good news first. Kai is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *An ordinary mirror*, Kai says, “I clean the mirrors on quiet mornings. I offered the widow those mornings before we decide who takes the glass.”
connections: Wynn Martin. The classmate trying the line hears how a chosen name ought to sound aloud.

reactions.situation: A pupil chooses another language halfway through the reading
reactions.response: Edward lets the pupil finish in the language they chose.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Edward repeats the correct name quietly, making the correction easy to hear without turning it into a performance.

reactions.situation: When pressed to explain someone else's silence
reactions.response: Edward says only what happened and lets the absent person keep their reasons.
